headline: Approved May meeting minutes; discussed line striping, Florida Ave traffic study, and Park Street watermain.
summary: Residents asked about line striping and a truck traffic study on Elm Street. The group discussed commission structure, the Florida Ave traffic calming petition, and the DPW 2026 priority work. The only vote recorded was to approve the May meeting minutes.
decisions: Approved the minutes from the May meeting unanimously.

8/27/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
MIC Members Present: Michelle Metzler, Chair; Micayla Schambura, Secretary; Gretchen 
Calcagni; Anna Vold
City Staff Present: Jon Rauscher, Public Works Director; Eli Ogilvie, City Councilor; Al Turkos, 
City Councilor
Guests Present: Terry Zigmund, Winooski resident
Call to Order by: Michelle
Meeting Start Time: 6:33 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Micayla
Public Comment
Terry Zigmund, resident of Winooski, inquired on the progress of freshening city-wide line 
striping, commenting that she was only seeing new paint on Main Street. This question included 
the bike lane on W Center Street, which she has been asking to be repainted for over 7 years.
Jon Rauscher, Public Works Director, replied that he put out a bid for linestriping work last 
month that would include Rt 15/East Allen. In general, corridors tend to have priority by 
contractors as local streets are done by DPW. One bid from a Massachusetts firm was 
submitted and priced at $40,000 to do all the white line striping (bike lane, fog lanes, and all of 
the white symbols and crosswalks with durable epoxy paint, the same kind of paint on Main 
Street). There is only $15,000 in Winooski’s line striping budget this year. The City is looking at 
reducing the scope of work and increasing the budget for next year.
Jon says that the City recently awarded a bid for a new walk-behind linestriping machine for 
internal DPW use. He says that depending on when the new machine arrives, he will coordinate 
with the DPW crew to see if they can stripe the bike lane on W Center street in-house, since it’s 
a shorter straight section (longer sections would require other equipment to keep the line 
straight).
Terry also wanted to follow up on the traffic calming study on West/Elm Street that was 
performed last year. The findings of the traffic calming study reported there were no large trucks 
during the data collection period. She is looking to see if there was any follow-up on restudying 
since it seemed like an anomaly that there was no truck traffic during this period.
Jon says that he is looking to request an additional truck traffic study on Elm Street, wrapped 
into a city-wide traffic calming study he secured as part of the FY27 budget. This city-wide traffic 
calming study has partial grant funding through CCRPC and will evaluate 10 additional streets 
that are in our traffic calming manuals. He says that he also heard that Cabot is taking full 
control of the industrial facility, and that they are very aware of the truck routes and conveying 
that to their drivers.
Terry says there has been an improvement in truck traffic speed as the smaller trucks that were 
driving very fast are no longer there. However, she is concerned that the trucks are too big and 
are hitting the curbs and destroying them. Jon says he is going to need to look further into this 
with other city staff, he agrees with her, but says it is a legacy issue that the industrial area was 
approved in a residential area. The Winooski Truck Traffic code does not specify maximum 
vehicle dimensions. For reference, Winooski’s Municipal Code Chapter 20 Truck Traffic Code is 
available here.
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Micayla
Second: Anna
Decision: Approve
The minutes from theMay meetingwere unanimously passed.
Discussion: Commission Reflection on What's Working, What's Not
Eli Ogilvie says that there have been internal discussions about what the City wants 
commissions to be, and what is/isn’t working. He says that a lot of work, intended for 
commissions, has gone to city staff. He asks what things we see as important to keep as we 
rethink commission structure.
Michelle Metzler says that it is unclear what council wants from commissions and that there is 
an illusion of participating as there are things the commission has worked hard on, and it did not 
feel like it received the support of the Council or Mayor. She says this disconnect can lead to 
struggling with participation and/or growth. Micayla Schambura joins the discussion about 
having more discrete tasks and focus would be beneficial – things that can be line-itemed as 
progress for the group.
Anna Vold, the newest member of the MIC, says that she likes the monthly frequency of the 
meetings as she sees tangible things happen (such as renovations around the City). She is 
interested in seeing what happens after our meetings and what impact she and the group can 
have.
Gretchen Calcagni joined the commission when Main St was underway. She says that because 
staff time is limited, it feels like agenda items are tough to move forward. She wonders if after 
these big infrastructure projects are complete that the meeting can have more action items 
once Winooski is back into more planning stages instead of construction.
Jon says that historically commission structure in Winooski is relatively new. Commissions 
were created when the City created new master plans and they were initially specialized 
thinktanks for Council. The Transportation Master Plan was the original cohort of 
commissioners’ main task.
Michelle says that Jon serving the liaison role as director of Public Works is very helpful for 
helping educate the commissioners and being able to answer questions during public comment. 
She wonders if other council members are staff who are aligned with their commission’s line of 
work. Eli says that department heads are the liaisons for the other commissions and have 
defined relations to it. He says for the Councilors, it is not a perfect match, but a lot of the 
councilors are interested in the topics that they are liaisons for.
Michelle comments on the idea of the Inclusion & Belonging Committee being instead integrated 
within groups, instead of making it separate. She says that singling it out may give the 
impression that other commissions aren’t functioning under DEI/I&BC principles. There should 
be people in all committees who believe in and act in support of these ideas. The group 
suggests that IB&C instead be a smaller task force every time there is a specific task item that 
comes up that needs addressed – it could pull from a list of Councilors or other citizens who are 
interested in DEI/IB&C to help fill the temporary role.
Eli poses the question on whether folks would prefer to have local wards / zoning, or combine all 
commissions into a singular commission. There was a mixed response to this question, but 
generally folks did not prefer having wards. Gretchen was not opposed to the idea of having 
location based groups like Burlington. Michelle, however, says that this seems more for 
community than joining out of interest. Micayla comments that if all groups have to meet with 
Council, this could stretch them and city staff out more. Al says that location-based groups 
could make Winooski more segregated.
Jon says that the current charter doesn’t reflect how commissions have ever served and 
recommends changing the charter to what we want the commission to be. He says it feels like 
commissions are transitioning more into outreach for the particular topics rather than technical 
work, and that staff is looking on guidance, too.
The group discusses creating a schedule of agenda topics for the fiscal year to have some 
structure (new budget starts). The group agrees that meetings should be regular so the public 
can expect consistency. They should be at least every other month, with additional meetings in 
between as needed.
Discussion: Traffic Calming Study, Petition, and Funding
A petition was filed by residents living on Florida Ave to get a traffic study done prior to repaving. 
The City has a traffic calming manual to create policy on how measures get implemented. We 
have a candidate list of submitted complaints, Florida Ave was on this list. The City had funds to 
do a city-wide traffic calming evaluation and concept planning for 10 streets. Jon submitted the 
candidate list of CCRPC in January, removing the streets previously studied and streets that are 
considered collector streets to target neighborhood streets, and eliminated George & Upper 
Franklin (try to do these when there is school traffic, the study would take place when there isn’t 
school during the summer).
These 10 streets, including Florida Ave, were studied this summer. CCRPC is putting together 
that data from the summer. We’ll have data for those ten streets including Florida Ave pretty 
soon, which will dictate whether each street will meet the threshold for traffic calming measures 
based on speed, truck traffic, and crashes. There will be a public outreach piece on this.
Discussion: DPW 2026 Season Priority Work
The following public works priority plan includes budgeted capital work and 2026-2027 policy. 
Work is mostly driven by the budget. Highlights include RFP Advertisement of the Burlington-
Winooski River Bridge Replacement Project, as well as the Hoods Crossing traffic signal and 
Spring sidewalk extension to be out to bid this winter. The Abenaki Parking Garage construction 
is coming to a close, but there is a punch list of items to get through. Other work is related to 
transportation, stormwater, and facilities/grounds. Water Distribution Master Plan just started -
evaluates priorities for replacement.
One need not in budget currently is to install watermain on Park Street due to Armory building 
project. It would require a water main service from each side to feed the sprinkler service. Some 
items on the current list will need to be deprioritized for this water main on Park St and repaving 
prior to building. The work may require a bond vote and further discussion will be necessary to 
determine what to deprioritize.
City Council Liaison Updates
There were no additional updates to tonight’s discussion.
Inclusion & Belonging Commission Update
N/A
City Staff Liaison Updates
There were no additional updates to tonight’s discussion.
Other Business
N/A
Adjourn
Motion by: Anna
Second: Micayla
Meeting End Time: 8:33 pm

Discussion: Commission Reflection on What's Working, What's Not
Eli Ogilvie says that there have been internal discussions about what the City wants 
commissions to be, and what is/isn’t working. He says that a lot of work, intended for 
commissions, has gone to city staff. He asks what things we see as important to keep as we 
rethink commission structure.
Michelle Metzler says that it is unclear what council wants from commissions and that there is 
an illusion of participating as there are things the commission has worked hard on, and it did not 
feel like it received the support of the Council or Mayor. She says this disconnect can lead to 
struggling with participation and/or growth. Micayla Schambura joins the discussion about 
having more discrete tasks and focus would be beneficial – things that can be line-itemed as 
progress for the group.
Anna Vold, the newest member of the MIC, says that she likes the monthly frequency of the 
meetings as she sees tangible things happen (such as renovations around the City). She is 
interested in seeing what happens after our meetings and what impact she and the group can 
have.
Gretchen Calcagni joined the commission when Main St was underway. She says that because 
staff time is limited, it feels like agenda items are tough to move forward. She wonders if after 
these big infrastructure projects are complete that the meeting can have more action items 
once Winooski is back into more planning stages instead of construction.
Jon says that historically commission structure in Winooski is relatively new. Commissions 
were created when the City created new master plans and they were initially specialized 
thinktanks for Council. The Transportation Master Plan was the original cohort of 
commissioners’ main task.
Michelle says that Jon serving the liaison role as director of Public Works is very helpful for 
helping educate the commissioners and being able to answer questions during public comment. 
She wonders if other council members are staff who are aligned with their commission’s line of 
work. Eli says that department heads are the liaisons for the other commissions and have 
defined relations to it. He says for the Councilors, it is not a perfect match, but a lot of the 
councilors are interested in the topics that they are liaisons for.
Michelle comments on the idea of the Inclusion & Belonging Committee being instead integrated 
within groups, instead of making it separate. She says that singling it out may give the 
impression that other commissions aren’t functioning under DEI/I&BC principles. There should 
be people in all committees who believe in and act in support of these ideas. The group 
suggests that IB&C instead be a smaller task force every time there is a specific task item that 
comes up that needs addressed – it could pull from a list of Councilors or other citizens who are 
interested in DEI/IB&C to help fill the temporary role.
Eli poses the question on whether folks would prefer to have local wards / zoning, or combine all 
commissions into a singular commission. There was a mixed response to this question, but 
generally folks did not prefer having wards. Gretchen was not opposed to the idea of having 
location based groups like Burlington. Michelle, however, says that this seems more for 
community than joining out of interest. Micayla comments that if all groups have to meet with 
Council, this could stretch them and city staff out more. Al says that location-based groups 
could make Winooski more segregated.
Jon says that the current charter doesn’t reflect how commissions have ever served and 
recommends changing the charter to what we want the commission to be. He says it feels like 
commissions are transitioning more into outreach for the particular topics rather than technical 
work, and that staff is looking on guidance, too.
The group discusses creating a schedule of agenda topics for the fiscal year to have some 
structure (new budget starts). The group agrees that meetings should be regular so the public 
can expect consistency. They should be at least every other month, with additional meetings in 
between as needed.
Discussion: Traffic Calming Study, Petition, and Funding
A petition was filed by residents living on Florida Ave to get a traffic study done prior to repaving. 
The City has a traffic calming manual to create policy on how measures get implemented. We 
have a candidate list of submitted complaints, Florida Ave was on this list. The City had funds to 
do a city-wide traffic calming evaluation and concept planning for 10 streets. Jon submitted the 
candidate list of CCRPC in January, removing the streets previously studied and streets that are 
considered collector streets to target neighborhood streets, and eliminated George & Upper 
Franklin (try to do these when there is school traffic, the study would take place when there isn’t 
school during the summer).
These 10 streets, including Florida Ave, were studied this summer. CCRPC is putting together 
that data from the summer. We’ll have data for those ten streets including Florida Ave pretty 
soon, which will dictate whether each street will meet the threshold for traffic calming measures 
based on speed, truck traffic, and crashes. There will be a public outreach piece on this.
Discussion: DPW 2026 Season Priority Work
The following public works priority plan includes budgeted capital work and 2026-2027 policy. 
Work is mostly driven by the budget. Highlights include RFP Advertisement of the Burlington-
Winooski River Bridge Replacement Project, as well as the Hoods Crossing traffic signal and 
Spring sidewalk extension to be out to bid this winter. The Abenaki Parking Garage construction 
is coming to a close, but there is a punch list of items to get through. Other work is related to 
transportation, stormwater, and facilities/grounds. Water Distribution Master Plan just started -
evaluates priorities for replacement.
One need not in budget currently is to install watermain on Park Street due to Armory building 
project. It would require a water main service from each side to feed the sprinkler service. Some 
items on the current list will need to be deprioritized for this water main on Park St and repaving 
prior to building. The work may require a bond vote and further discussion will be necessary to 
determine what to deprioritize.
